official.citizenship_residency: Open to leaders from around the world; there is no citizenship restriction published, but master's fellowship recipients may not study at a Rotary Peace Center in their home country.
official.international_eligibility: Open to applicants worldwide; eight Rotary Peace Centers operate across the USA, Japan, England, Australia, Sweden, Uganda, Türkiye and India.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Fellowships cannot be used for doctoral study. Certificate candidates must meet the regional criteria of their chosen partner: Africa for Makerere University, the Middle East or North Africa for Bahçeşehir University, and Asia for Symbiosis International University.
official.research_requirement: Master's candidates must be able to undertake extensive reading and research, and present their master's research at a final seminar; the master's programme includes a self-designed two- to three-month field study.
official.duration: Master's programmes last 15 to 24 months and include a two- to three-month field study; the certificate programme is a one-year blended learning course requiring 11 weeks of on-site participation
official.description: The Rotary Peace Fellowship, funded by The Rotary Foundation, awards up to 170 fellowships a year for leaders with work experience in peace and development to study at one of eight Rotary Peace Centers.
official.program_type: Fully funded postgraduate fellowship in peace and development studies
official.english_requirement: Master's and certificate candidates must be proficient in English, and all applications and recommendations must be submitted in English.

applicant_utility.summary: This is one of the few fully funded fellowships that states its coverage in a single line: tuition and fees, room and board, round-trip transportation, and internship and field-study expenses, so there is no hidden gap you have to bridge beyond personal spending. Choose your track deliberately, because the master's route needs only three years of relevant experience but a three-year gap since your last degree, while the certificate route needs five years of experience and a social change initiative you bring with you. Note the two hard structural limits: the fellowship cannot fund doctoral study, and master's fellows may not study at a Rotary Peace Center in their own country. With only up to 50 master's and up to 120 certificate places a year across eight centres, the real competition is for a place at a specific partner university rather than for the fellowship in the abstract.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Mid-career peace and development professionals who can show sustained relevant work experience and who want a funded degree or certificate without a financial contribution.
application_readiness_checklist: Count your full-time relevant experience against the three-year master's or five-year certificate threshold before choosing a track
Check the three-year rule: if you finished a degree recently, or are enrolled now or in the coming academic year, you are not eligible
Confirm you are not an active Rotary member or employee of a Rotary entity, and check the three-year wait if you previously held a Rotary Peace Centers award or Global Grant Scholarship
Reach out to a Rotary club or district early, since clubs and districts help recruit candidates even though they are not required to fund them
For the certificate track, arrive with a concrete social change initiative and align your region with the partner you name
common_rejection_risks: Applying while still enrolled in an undergraduate or graduate programme, or in the upcoming academic year, which makes the applicant ineligible
Naming a Rotary Peace Center in your own country for a master's fellowship, which is not permitted
Assuming the fellowship can fund doctoral study, which it cannot
For the certificate track, naming a partner whose regional criteria you do not meet, such as Makerere for those without Africa links
Being an active Rotary member or Rotary employee, which is an absolute bar rather than a scoring penalty
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Personal spending beyond room, board and the covered travel, internship and field-study costs. Rotary does not publish a stipend or living allowance figure, so budget for incidental costs from your own resources.
document_audit: Everything, including recommendations, must be in English, so a non-English recommendation needs translating before submission
The relevant experience definition is specific, so map your roles against Rotary's relevant experience eligibility guide rather than assuming any development job counts
Certificate candidates must be able to explain how their plan to promote peace aligns with Rotary's mission, not just their own goals
The partner-university regional criteria are assessed at application, so changing centre later is not a neutral administrative switch
alerts: The 2027-28 application is closed and the 2028-29 application only becomes available online in February 2027, so prepare documents now and submit as soon as the portal opens
A club or district recommendation is supported but not required, so a lack of Rotary connections is not disqualifying
A new Rotary Peace Center at Symbiosis International University in Pune, India is opening in 2027 and will widen the Asia regional option for certificate candidates
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Application submitted online to The Rotary Foundation when the cycle opens in February, with a Rotary club or district recommendation where available; applications are reviewed by Rotary Peace Centers staff and qualified applications move forward for further consideration.
